author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This parser reads Cortex Xpanse attack surface (ASM) alerts, one JSON record per alert. The example bridge in bridges/cortex-xpanse-alerts pulls them from the Get Alerts API and posts them to HTTP Ingest. Each alert goes to Thirdparty, since Sophos Fusion has no vulnerability or exposure schema for custom parsers.
notes:
Setup:
- Cortex Xpanse forwards alerts only by email, Slack or syslog, and Palo Alto documents no syslog format for them.
- This parser reads the records the example bridge in bridges/cortex-xpanse-alerts pulls from the Get Alerts API and posts to HTTP Ingest: one JSON record per attack surface (ASM) alert, as Xpanse returns it, with "xpanse_record" and the tenant first.
- Give the bridge an advanced API key whose role can view alerts and use the public API.
- Each alert is sent once, when Xpanse stores it; a later status change isn't sent again.

Field mapping:
- Sophos Fusion has no vulnerability or exposure schema for custom parsers, so each alert goes to Thirdparty, the schema the Sophos Fusion schema list gives alerts from sources outside Sophos Fusion.
- Thirdparty takes the name as the title, the description as the summary, alert_id, the resolution status (such as STATUS_010_NEW), the attack surface rule name as the category, informational, low, medium, high and critical as info, low, medium, high and critical, the first IPv4 address (or IPv6 address), the first domain, the port and protocol as the target, and the detection, change and last observed times.
- The rule ID, external ID, alert categories, remediation guidance, every address and domain, tags, asset and service IDs, cloud providers, the certificate's subject and issuer, MITRE techniques and the case ID go to additional_data.
- Xpanse returns the address, domain and tag lists as JSON arrays; a comma-joined string, which other Xpanse endpoints use, works too.

Time:
- The event time is when Xpanse detected the issue.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the shapes of the Get Alerts schema in Palo Alto's REST API reference and the alert examples in Palo Alto's XSOAR integration tests, with documentation addresses and names under example.com, example.net and example.org.
- The tenant in xpanse_tenant is written under example.com because the repo's sample scan blocks other host names.

Testing:
- Passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-22 (99 of 99 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs).
- No built-in parser claimed these records.
